key_insight: A backward-mapping, genome-guided workflow can translate device targets into chemically interpretable design rules to discover phase-stable, lead-free double perovskites.
engineering_relevance: The approach narrows a 13,088-composition search space to DFT-validated candidates, offering a practical inverse-design pipeline for safer optoelectronic materials.
method: Filtered 13,088 charge-balanced A2BB'X6 compositions with halide-aware geometric formability rules.
Encoded six families of chemical-genome descriptors and trained evolutionary-optimized ML surrogates for stability and band gap.
Used SHAP interpretation plus DFT phenotype closure to validate seven lead-free candidate double perovskites.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a pipeline validated on Ehull-derived stability labels and DFT checks, yielding seven candidates with confirmed structural, electronic, optical, and transport properties.
watch_item: The band-gap surrogate is trained on scalar-relativistic PBE values, so predictions may shift relative to higher-level methods or experiment.
paper_title: Backward Mapping from Device Targets to Chemical Genomes for Interpretable Discovery of Phase-Stable Lead-Free Double Perovskites with DFT-Validated Design Rules
